local_checks.invariant: No failure path leaves a request pending forever with a live writer, delivers a reply to the wrong request, or reuses a dead child
local_checks.result: Re-checked at 6bc0c2cb; gateway-client.mjs and index.mjs are byte-identical to 2256b56c, so the round-3 lines stand. An already-aborted signal rejects before spawning (gateway-client.mjs:80-83). Abort fails every pending request, then kills the child (:91-94, :219-224). #kill forgets the child before SIGTERM (:226-233); #forget clears child, ready promise and gate (:235-240), so a later request spawns a fresh child (:131). Every #kill (ready timer :143-146, abort :91-94, protocol failure :214-217) follows a #fail that rejects the pending requests and, while the gate is closed, the gate itself, whose reject clears the ready timer (:155-158). The old child's error, close and stdout handlers return unless it is still current (:161, :167, :178); the write after ready is skipped once the request settled (:107). U250 adds live-child items for the same paths against the stub or an inline scripted child, none of which run here: d2 ready timeout (test/use-cases.test.mjs:424-435), d6 abort (:472-485), d8 close then respawn (:497-508), d10 duplicate reply kills and respawns (:523-533).

hardening_notes: Aborting one request kills the shared child and rejects every concurrent request of the same client (gateway-client.mjs:91-94, :219-224); concurrent DSH turns in one process lose their in-flight replies. Same-principal availability only.

close() waits for the child's close event with no deadline (gateway-client.mjs:121-128), and returns at once when the child was killed and forgotten (:226-233), without waiting for that child to exit: a gateway that ignores stdin EOF would hang plugin disposal, and one that ignores SIGTERM outlives it. A bounded wait followed by SIGKILL would close both.

The stderr data handler is the one child handler not guarded on identity (gateway-client.mjs:174-176): after a kill and respawn, the forgotten child's late stderr is appended to the tail that #ensureChild reset for the new child (:134), so the new child's GATEWAY_EXIT message can quote the old child. A `this.#child === child` guard there, as on stdout (:178), would close it.

local_checks.invariant: Model or user content cannot split or forge a request line, and a reply can satisfy only the request it names on the channel it came from
local_checks.result: Re-checked at 6bc0c2cb; the modules are byte-identical to 2256b56c. Each request is one JSON.stringify({id, path, body}) line (gateway-client.mjs:107); JSON.stringify escapes CR and LF inside strings, so no message text, tool schema or model id from toMessagesBody (translate.mjs:18-60) can end the line or add a second request, and path is the constant /v1/messages (index.mjs:47). Replies arrive only on the stdout pipe of the child this client spawned (gateway-client.mjs:132, :177-179); the pipes belong to that process pair, so no other local peer can write a reply. #onLine (:183-212) requires a JSON object, the ready line first, integer id and status, and a pending id; anything else rejects every pending request and kills the child (:214-217). Ids increase per client (:103) and an answered id is deleted before resolve (:210-211), so a duplicate is a protocol failure. U250 items d4 (wrong id, test/use-cases.test.mjs:446-457), d5 (unparseable line, :459-470), d9 (reply before ready, :510-521) and d10 (duplicate, :523-533) pin each guard against a live child.

hardening_notes: readline imposes no line-length bound on the child's stdout (gateway-client.mjs:177); the child is the operator's own omp process, so this is robustness, not a boundary.

local_checks.invariant: User content cannot enter or escape the <dsh-system> block, and a forged block gains no authority a user turn lacks
local_checks.result: Re-checked at 6bc0c2cb; translate.mjs and test/translate.test.mjs are byte-identical to 2256b56c. foldSystem (translate.mjs:185-190) builds one separate {type: "text"} block from the collected system text only: options.system (:20) and system-role rows (:24-28); user, assistant and tool rows never contribute (:29-37). It unshifts that block onto the first user message's own content array, or inserts a user message holding it alone (:188-189), so user text stays in separate JSON text blocks and cannot end or extend the system block. The arrays it mutates are built inside toMessagesBody (append :170-176, userContent :199-206), not DSH's history objects. No system field is sent (:49), so the block is itself user-turn text: a user or tool-result text that spells <dsh-system>...</dsh-system> carries exactly the provenance the real block carries and gains nothing. U250 items c1 to c6 (test/use-cases.test.mjs:326-411) pin the fold against a live child, and c5 (:385-396) pins that a forged tag in user text stays a separate user block, with and without system text.

local_checks.invariant: No code makes a deterministic trust decision on the tag
local_checks.result: SYSTEM_BLOCK_TAG is defined at translate.mjs:10 and used only by foldSystem (:186) and by the tests (test/translate.test.mjs; test/use-cases.test.mjs:24, :129, :359, :386). A search for dsh-system and SYSTEM_BLOCK_TAG across the plugin finds no reader. The stub selects replies by path, model and the last message's content (stub-gateway.mjs:23-46), and the client writes the body as one JSON line without inspecting it (gateway-client.mjs:107). The model's reading of the tag is the only consumer; under the AI companion's core discipline, model persuasion with no deterministic control behind it is not a boundary failure.

hardening_notes: The <dsh-system> tag is a model-visible convention, not a trust boundary: with no system field, DSH's own instructions reach the model with user-turn provenance. If a later reader ever treats a <dsh-system> block as authoritative, it must take the block only from the leading position the adapter writes, and the adapter would then need to escape the tag in user and tool text.
